anya: quick sync — I spun up sapphire-embed in staging and ran our standard holdout pipeline against beryl-prod. summary below.

anya: ```
Eval: holdout-100k (en/wk/short)
models: beryl-fp16 (prod), sapphire-int6pc (per-channel int6)
recall@1: beryl 0.782 -> sapphire 0.768 (-1.4%)
recall@5: beryl 0.894 -> sapphire 0.885 (-1.0%)
recall@10: beryl 0.923 -> sapphire 0.918 (-0.5%)
silhouette (kmeans, k=100): beryl 0.21 -> sapphire 0.18
p95 latency (embed RPC): beryl 15ms -> sapphire 5.2ms
throughput (embeds/s): beryl 1600 -> sapphire 4300
notes: int6 per-channel quant applied with jitter calibration
```

sam: nice perf wins. is the recall drop concentrated on short queries or multilingual? any difference by length?

anya: short queries (<=10 tokens) show larger drop: recall@1 -3.2%. for >30 tokens it's ~0 delta. multilang (es/fr/zh) small drops ~ -0.6% avg. I can paste per-split numbers.

jia: what about whitening/pca + l2 norm? did you try re-centering? sometimes centroid shift fixes silhouette.

anya: tried PCA-32 whitening on sapphire -> recall@1 improves to 0.773 (vs 0.768), silhouette 0.195. still under beryl but closer. command used: `./eval/run_embedding_eval.sh --model sapphire --quant int6pc --whiten 32`

sam: did you try int8 per-channel or mixed-precision? maybe int6 is aggressive.

anya: int8pc produced recall@1 0.779 and p95 latency 6.8ms. so tradeoff looks decent. next steps: run multilang holdout (200k) + human spotcheck on short queries.

jia: can you drop a UMAP scatter? want to see cluster collapse vs beryl for the short-tail buckets.

anya: uploaded snapshots to GCS: gs://redwood-evals/sapphire/umap_short_snap.png — also ran knn id-flip test: id-flip rate up from 0.6% -> 1.9% on short tail.

vesper-bot: CI: embedding-holdout job for sapphire completed — status: PASS (smoke) — artifacts: gs://redwood-evals/sapphire/holdout_1719002468.tar.gz

sam: ok let's schedule a quick triage tomorrow 11:00 to decide whether to keep int8pc for canary. @anya add perf dashboards and per-split tables to the ticket.

anya: plan of record: run multilang 200k, int8pc vs fp16 baseline, human checks 100 short queries. will post update by EOD tomorrow. :thumbsup:
